0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard was adopted bythe Indian Standards Institution on 29 January 1976, after the draft finalized by the Compressors Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 The need for a standard on air receivers for compressed air installations has been felt for quite sometime by Jhe air compressors industry. This standard has been formulated keeping in view the international practices in this field. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, obtained from the leading manufacturers considerable assistance has been and users in this country.

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement o this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3.1 Air

receivers help to dampen actions and shall help to condense moisture in the compressed air, and settle down before air passes into the

3.2 Air receiver shall provide a `~flywheel effect `, that is, it shall meet the varying demands without compressor regulation functioning incessantly. Air receivers are, therefore, also used for storage of air. 4. LOCATION 4.1 In order to obtain as much cooling effect as possible the receiver shall preferably be installed outdoors or in an open shed. It shall be supported off the ground to prevent rusting. 4.1.1 In a long distribution line it pays to instal one or more receivers farther on in the system or at a point of intermittent heavy demand. 5. SIZE 5.1 The capacity of the receiver shall be one-tenth of the free air delivery per minute of the compressor, increasing with smaller compressors to about one-sixth. This should be regarded as a minimum. A much bigger capacity shall be needed to provide any appreciable storage of air. This is not applicable to portable compressors. In the case of rotary compressors, .a receiver of this capacity shall be in addition to the receiver forming part of the compressor design. 5.1.1 If the air receiver is also to be used for storage followin-g formula may be used for determining its size: T= where 7 = time in hours receiver supplies air from upper pressure limits; V = volume of receiver in ma; PO = atmospheric pressure in bar; to lower of air, the

P, = maximum pressure, absolute in bar ( compressor discharge pressure ) ; Pn = minimum receiver pressure, absolute in bar ( pressure required to operate tool ); and C= amount of free air drawn per hour in ms ( from study of local cycle ).

6. MANUFACTURE 6.1 Air receivers shall' be manufactured according to IS : 28%1969* but the design pressure shall be assumed as maximum working pressure plus 10 percent. Receivers up to a pressure of 3.5 bar shall be regarded as Class111 vessels and those with higher pressures as Class II.
*Code for unfired pressure vessels.

IS:7938 - 1976
7. MOUNTINGS 7.1 Safety Valve - Each air receiver shall be provided with a safety valve preferably `of the direct spring loaded type and shall be so constructed and adjusted as to permit the air to-escape from the air receiver without increasing the pressure beyond 10 percent above the working pressure when the air compressor or compressors are givmg full output and all outlets other than safety valve or valves are closed. It shall be 7.1.1 Safety valves shall be fitted with hand lifting gear. possible to lift the valve spindle at a pressure not less than 75 percent of working pressures. 7.1.2 Safety valves shall be fitted with a protecting cap or under the adjusting screw, so that they cannot be inadvertently loaded beyond the pressure at which they have been adjusted. ferrule over-

7.2 Drain Valve - A drain valve or cock shall be provided either for at a point for enabling the draining of manual or automatic operation, the condensate. 7.3 Pressure GaugeA pressure gauge shall be fitted to each receiver. The bourdon type of gauge conforming to IS : 3624-1966* is The dial shall be graduated in bar and the graduation recommended. shall be from zero to not less than one-and-half times, and not more than twice the design pressure of the receiver. 7.4 Fusible PlugsFusible installation in case of excessive plugs may be fitted to safeguard rise in temperature due to fire. be such the that

7.4.1 The position of fusible plug where fitted shall discharge of the plug will not do injury to any person. 8. ACCESS 8.1 Each AND INSPECTION OPENINGS air receiver

9.2 Hydraulic Test - Every receiver shall be tested at the manufacturer's works by hydraulic pressure to 1.5 times the design pressure. While under pressure the air receiver shall be struck with a hammer on both sides and close to welded seams and a thorough examination made. The pressure shall be maintained for 10 minutes. 10. INSTALLATION for the receiver and the support shall be IO.1 Proper foundation details provided by the manufacturer. 11. SURFACE TREATMENT shall be given inside and outside
